key_insight: In simulated clinical prediction networks, reliable LLM auditing depended on computation and explicit instructions, not direct access to model weights.
clinical_relevance: Tool-assisted LLMs may help identify learned relationships and subgroup bias in clinical prediction models, but real-world clinical usefulness remains untested.
method: Trained networks with 105–38,401 weights on simulated subarachnoid haemorrhage cohorts with planted relationships or no relationship.
Compared five GPT models using raw weights without tools versus calculation tools with weight or prediction-only access.
Tested default versus explicit instructions, subgroup death under-recording, and a scripted comparator.
evidence_signal: With calculation tools, GPT-6 Astra recovered planted relationships in 29/29 runs, raised no false alarms in 15 null-network runs, and identified the biased subgroup in 6/6 runs; prediction-only access matched weight access.
watch_item: These simulation results do not establish clinical validity, and a well-designed script matched comparator-model audits and the best LLM repair.
paper_title: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks
